text:
Tanya: Quick ask from growth — they need a short eu-central GPU burst for a customer demo next Tue. Vendor says racks are available but nodes must be on firmware >=3.9 to support our NVLink layout. Two quick things: 1) can infra validate topology compatibility without changes? 2) procurement: how will burst reservations be billed (on-demand vs reservation)?

Josh: For topology we need exact firmware build and whether the vendor will apply our fusion/axiom patches during the flash. If it's just >=3.9 we're usually fine, but mismatched NVLink config shows up in the microbench. Can someone share rack serials?

Marco: I already asked the vendor and pasted the convo below. Also asked about billing model. Waiting for finance/legal confirmation.

Tanya: Also, if this is a burst pool can we enforce a hard per-tenant cap so Growth can't spill into production pools? I started a proto TF var in a draft PR.

Carla: ping @carla for a quick TF review when you have a sec: PR #612 (modules/gpu/pools 1 add eu-burst policy). Snippet: 
```
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "./modules/gpu"
  name   = "eu-burst-apr26"
  max_tenants = 4
  reserved_hours = 180
}
```

Emily: We can enforce quota via the policy server using tenant labels. I'll add a deny rule: "deny if tenant != growth and pool == eu-burst". I can push a patch in ~2hrs.

Marco: Vendor reply (copied): "PO 1023 acknowledged. Firmware 3.9.x available on racks R22-R24. Burst reservations billed as on-demand + 15% reservation surcharge unless a monthly commit is signed. Firmware flash window proposed: 2026-04-06 02:00-06:00 UTC. R22-R24 are isolated from other customers."

Josh: That means performance variability until flash completes. Recommend we run a canary smoke after the flash and have an automated fallback mapping to west-eu pool. Tanya, can Growth accept the flash window? If not, we spin up a temporary west-eu run.

Tanya: Growth accepts the window but asks for verification steps post-flash. Can infra run a 10-min nvlink smoke and a small gen workload? If smoke fails, fallback to west-eu.

Josh: Yep. I'll add a canary job in the pipeline. Command I plan to use: 
```
./deploy_canary.sh --pool eu-burst-apr26 --smoke nvlink-basic --fallback west-eu-burst
```

Marco: Also asked vendor to confirm whether the reservation counts toward any committed quotas on their portal. They reiterated the invoice model above and said commits need a signed monthly addendum. Legal wants a draft by Fri 2026-04-03.

Vendor-bot: PO 1023 status: acknowledged. Firmware window scheduled for 2026-04-06 02:00-06:00 UTC. Billing: on-demand + 15% surcharge unless monthly commit is signed.

Carla: Reviewed PR #612 1 left small comments on var naming and defaulting. I'll push a follow-up after Tanya confirms the policy rule. ETA ~1hr.

Emily: MR #618 prepared for the deny rule, will hold for the canary run and will monitor token-level cost during the smoke.

Marco: Update: vendor confirmed racks are isolated and accepts our PO terms for the one-off. Finance/Legal to review commit language.

Tanya: Filing a weekly follow-up item and tagging infra/procure: @Josh @Marco @Carla @Emily. Please post when vendor confirms billing type and when the firmware window is locked. I'll tell Growth to expect a canary run right after the flash. :thumbsup:

Josh: I'll kick the canary pipeline after the flash and drop logs here. :white_check_mark:

Vendor-bot: Reminder: please confirm PO acceptance terms by 2026-04-03 to lock monthly commit pricing.
